Density-based clustering: DBSCAN and HDBSCAN

Source: R/seg_cluster.R
seg_cluster_density.Rd

Finds dense regions of respondents with DBSCAN (dbscan::dbscan()) or HDBSCAN (dbscan::hdbscan()) and labels respondents outside of them as noise (cluster 0). Requires the dbscan package.

Usage

seg_cluster_density(
  x,
  method = c("dbscan", "hdbscan"),
  eps = NULL,
  min_pts = NULL,
  plots = TRUE,
  cluster_plot_args = list(),
  dend_args = list(),
  centers_args = list(),
  heatmap_n = 200,
  seed = 123,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

The output of seg_prep_data() (recommended), or a data frame or numeric matrix with already prepared clustering variables (no missing values).

method

"dbscan" (default) or "hdbscan".

eps

Radius of the neighborhood for DBSCAN. NULL (default) uses the knee of the k-nearest-neighbor distance plot (see seg_dbscan_eps()).

min_pts

Minimum number of respondents in the neighborhood of a core point (DBSCAN) or minimum cluster size (HDBSCAN). NULL (default) uses twice the number of clustering variables.

plots

Logical. Whether to create the plots. Defaults to TRUE.

cluster_plot_args

A list of arguments passed to factoextra::fviz_cluster(), overriding the defaults (see seg_plot_cluster()), e.g. list(ellipse.type = "convex").

dend_args

A list of arguments passed to factoextra::fviz_dend(), overriding the defaults (see seg_plot_dend()), e.g. list(type = "phylogenic").

centers_args

A list of arguments passed to seg_plot_centers(), overriding the defaults, e.g. list(type = "bars", scale = "original").

heatmap_n

Number of respondents randomly sampled for the heatmap. Defaults to 200.

seed

Random seed. The global random seed is left untouched. Defaults to 123.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print the results. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

For a single number of clusters, an object of class seg_cluster, a list with the elements:

  • method, family: the clustering method and its family.

  • k: the requested number of clusters (NA for density-based methods).

  • k_found: the number of clusters found (excluding noise).

  • cluster: integer vector with the cluster of each respondent (0 = noise), in the order of the prepared data.

  • membership: matrix with the membership degrees (fuzzy) or probabilities (model-based) of each respondent in each cluster, NULL for the other methods.

  • sizes: tibble with the size and share of each cluster.

  • centers: tibble with the mean of each clustering variable per cluster.

  • assignment: tibble with the respondent identifier, the cluster and method-specific information (e.g. the highest membership degree).

  • data, data_full, dist: the prepared clustering variables, the original data of the retained respondents and the distance matrix (if available), as passed on from seg_prep_data().

  • fit: the result of the underlying clustering function.

  • tree: the hierarchical tree (class hclust) for hierarchical methods and hierarchical k-means, otherwise NULL.

  • cluster_map: named integer vector mapping the cluster codes of fit (names) to the renumbered codes, NULL if not renumbered.

  • prep: the preparation settings of seg_prep_data() (variables, missing values, rescaling parameters), used to prepare new respondents in predict.seg_cluster().

  • plots: list of plots (see "Visualizations").

  • settings: list of the settings used.

For several numbers of clusters, an object of class seg_cluster_set, a list with the elements solutions (named list of seg_cluster objects, e.g. solutions$k4), summary (tibble with the cluster sizes per solution), plot (the cluster plots of all solutions combined) and method.

Details

DBSCAN

DBSCAN (density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise) does not need the number of clusters, but two parameters: the radius eps and the minimum number of points min_pts.

  1. A respondent is a core point if at least min_pts respondents (including itself) lie within the distance eps.

  2. Core points within eps of each other are connected and form a cluster; respondents within eps of a core point (border points) are added to its cluster.

  3. All other respondents are noise (cluster 0).

DBSCAN finds clusters of arbitrary shape and identifies outliers, but uses a single density threshold for all clusters. min_pts defaults to twice the number of clustering variables (a common rule of thumb). eps defaults to the "knee" of the sorted k-nearest-neighbor distances, see seg_dbscan_eps().

HDBSCAN

HDBSCAN (hierarchical DBSCAN) runs DBSCAN for all values of eps at once, builds a hierarchy of the resulting clusters and keeps the most stable clusters. It only needs min_pts (the minimum cluster size) and can find clusters of varying density. It also returns the probability of each respondent to belong to its cluster (assignment$membership_prob) and an outlier score (assignment$outlier_score, higher = more outlying).

When to use

For data with dense, well separated groups of arbitrary shape, and to detect outliers. Survey data with many correlated rating scales rarely contains such dense regions: the methods then find a single cluster (with some noise) or only noise. They are therefore mainly useful to identify outliers (e.g. to exclude them before a k-means or PAM segmentation) rather than for the segmentation itself. With many clustering variables, distances become similar for all respondents ("curse of dimensionality"), which makes density-based clustering difficult; consider clustering on a few principal components instead. The distance matrix of seg_prep_data() is used if available.

See also

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("dbscan", quietly = TRUE)) {
  prep <- seg_prep_data(iris, vars = -Species, verbose = FALSE)
  db <- seg_cluster_density(prep, eps = 0.8, min_pts = 8)
  db$sizes
}
#> 
#> ── Cluster solution: DBSCAN, k = 2 ──
#> 
#> • Cluster 1: n = 94 (63%)
#> • Cluster 2: n = 48 (32%)
#> • Noise: n = 8 (5%)
#> Plots: `$plots$cluster`, `$plots$heatmap`, and `$plots$centers`
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   cluster     n  share
#>     <int> <int>  <dbl>
#> 1       1    94 0.627 
#> 2       2    48 0.32  
#> 3       0     8 0.0533
# }
